title: Purity of coordinate divisors in the standard semistable trait model
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a Noetherian local domain of dimension one and principal maximal ideal; a uniformizer $\pi$ generates that maximal ideal. Suppose $\ell$ is invertible in $R$ and $n\geq1$. Put
$$X=\operatorname{Spec}R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(T_1\cdots T_n-\pi).$$
For every $i$ let $h_i:H_i\hookrightarrow X$ be the closed immersion cut out by $T_i=0$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The Cartier Kummer fundamental class induces an isomorphism
$$A_{H_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}h_i^!A_X(1)[2].$$
The assertion holds over any trait, without excellence, completion or henselianity assumptions.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.5.12 proof, printed p.251, all-one semistable case, with Lemma 3.5.13(iv). The source cites Illusie (2004), Theorem 1.4, and Rapoport--Zink (1982), Satz 2.21.

proof.text: Fix $i$. Apply [lem-per-primitive-monomial-trait-geometry] with every exponent equal to $1$ to see that $B=R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(T_1\cdots T_n-\pi)$ is a Noetherian regular domain. The coefficient map $R\to B$ is injective: a nonzero multiple of $T_1\cdots T_n-\pi$ in the polynomial ring has positive total degree, so cannot be a nonzero constant. Thus $\pi\ne0$ in $B$, and $T_1\cdots T_n=\pi$ implies every $T_i\ne0$. Hence $T_i$ is a nonzerodivisor and defines an effective Cartier divisor. The quotient is explicitly $B/(T_i)=\kappa(s)[T_1,\ldots,\widehat T_i,\ldots,T_n]$. This also covers $n=1$, where $X=S$ and $H_1=s$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(i) and the all-one case of Proposition 3.5.12, pp.250--251; elementary quotient computation.

proof.text: Let $\bar x$ be any geometric point of $H_i$, let $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$, $g:Y=\operatorname{Spec}C\to X$ the strict localization, $t_i$ the image of $T_i$, $D=V(t_i)$ with $h_D:D\hookrightarrow Y$, and $V=Y-D$. By Step 1, $B$ is regular and $B/(T_i)$ is a polynomial ring over the field $\kappa(s)$, hence regular by [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base]; $t_i$ is not a unit because $\bar x$ lies over $V(T_i)$. So [lem-sbc-strict-hensel-regular-divisor-quotient] gives that $C$ is Noetherian and $C/(t_i)$ is a regular domain. As $T_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $B$ and etale $B$-algebras are flat [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], $t_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on the filtered colimit $C$: $D$ is effective Cartier. By [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian], $D=H_i\times_XY$ is the strict localization of $H_i$ at $\bar x$; $Y$ and $D$ are strictly henselian local by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure]. Since $g$ is affine and ind-etale and $X,Y$ are Noetherian, [lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change] gives $(h_i^!A_X(1))|_D\simeq h_D^!A_Y(1)$, compatibly with the closed counits; the strict-local compatibility of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] (equivalently the pullback clause of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]) carries the class of $H_i$ to the class of $D\subset Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] and [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-etale-acyclic], $\Gamma(D,-)$ is exact and equals the stalk at $\bar x$, so $\mathcal H^q(h_i^!A_X(1)[2])_{\bar x}=H^{q}R\Gamma(D,h_D^!A_Y(1)[2])$, and by the derived closed adjunction $Rh_{D*}\dashv h_D^!$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] this is $\operatorname{Hom}(h_{D*}A_D,A_Y(1)[q+2])$, with $\eta$ corresponding to the transposed class. So it suffices that $H^q\,R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(h_{D*}A_D,A_Y(1))$ vanishes for $q\ne2$ and is generated by the class of $D$ for $q=2$.

source.place: Strict-local reduction of the semistable input on p.251; agent expansion by ind-etale closed-support base change and exact strict-local sections.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-semistable-coordinate-kummer-tower-acyclic] with $m=0$ to the schemes $V_r=\operatorname{Spec}(C[1/t_i,u_r]/(u_r^{\ell^r}-t_i))$. It supplies $H^0(V_r,A)=A$ by constant sections and $\varinjlim_rH^q(V_r,A)=0$ for all $q>0$. By [lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity], choose compatible primitive roots $\zeta_{\ell^r}$ in $C$: their residues exist in its separably closed residue field and lift uniquely after each residue choice since $\ell$ is invertible; choose them inductively with $\zeta_{\ell^{r+1}}^\ell=\zeta_{\ell^r}$. Then $a\in\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ acts by $u_r\mapsto\zeta_{\ell^r}^a u_r$. Each $V_r\to V$ is a finite etale surjective torsor: [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] applies to its monic root polynomial; its monic equation gives a free algebra of rank $\ell^r$, its derivative $\ell^r u_r^{\ell^r-1}$ is invertible. In its self-product the ratio $z$ of the roots satisfies $z^{\ell^r}=1$. The roots-of-unity node says the differences of distinct roots are units, so the Chinese remainder decomposition of $z^{\ell^r}-1=\prod_a(z-\zeta_{\ell^r}^a)$ identifies this self-product with a disjoint union indexed by $a$. Thus the self-product is the disjoint union of the graphs of these actions. The actions commute with $u_r=u_{r+1}^{\ell}$.

source.place: The semistable Kummer-cover calculation underlying the input cited on p.251; agent expansion.

proof.text: The tower therefore satisfies [lem-per-procyclic-torsor-tower-descent]. Its spectral sequence has only the row $b=0$, with trivial coefficient module $A$, so $H^q(V,A)=H^q_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathbf Z_\ell,A)$. Apply [lem-exc-procyclic-two-term] with $s=1$: the generator acts trivially, hence its two-term complex is $[A\xrightarrow0 A]$ in degrees $0,1$. It follows that $H^0(V,A)=A$, $H^1(V,A)=A$ and all higher groups vanish. The normalized degree-one edge of the descent node identifies the generator with the torsor $u_1^\ell=t_i$. Under the torsor/cohomology comparison [lem-sc-torsor-h1] and the Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base], its class is $\delta(t_i)\in H^1(V,\mu_\ell)=H^1(V,A(1))$. Our chosen roots identify $A(1)$ with the constant line; thus $\delta(t_i)$ is a basis of that one-dimensional group, and the restriction $H^0(Y,A(1))\to H^0(V,A(1))$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Agent Cartan--Leray and procyclic expansion of the semistable input cited by Proposition 3.5.12.

proof.text: Use [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] for $D\subset Y$ and $K=A_Y(1)$. It identifies the supported section complex with $\operatorname{Cone}(R\Gamma(Y,A(1))\to R\Gamma(V,A(1)))[-1]$. Since $Y$ is strictly henselian, [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-etale-acyclic] gives no positive cohomology on $Y$; Step 4 computes the other vertex and its degree-zero restriction. The long exact sequence of this cone gives zero in every degree except $2$, and its boundary $H^1(V,A(1))\to H^2_D(Y,A(1))$ is an isomorphism. In particular the boundary of $\delta(t_i)$ generates the degree-two supported group.

source.place: Agent localization argument following the semistable input cited on p.251.

proof.text: On $Y$ the line bundle $\mathcal O_Y(D)=(t_i)^\vee$ has the global frame $t_i^\vee$, and its divisor section is $\tau=t_i\,t_i^\vee$. Take $N=\ell$ and let $(\tau,E,f)$ be the data of [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary] for the supported Kummer map $c_{D,A}$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. Then $s=f(t_i^\vee)\in E(Y)$ lies over $1$, and on $V$ equivariance and $f(\tau)=0$ give $s|_V=f(t_i^{-1}\tau)=a(t_i^{-1})$. So $(g,m)\mapsto a(g)+ms$ kills the image of $1\mapsto(t_i^{-1},-1)$ of $j_!\mathbf Z_V$ and defines a map of extensions, identity on both ends, from the pushout $e_{t_i^{-1}}$ of [lem-per-supported-yoneda-localization] to $E$; thus $[E]=e_{t_i^{-1}}$. For the Kummer sequence with class $k$, that node gives that $k[1]\circ e_{t_i^{-1}}$ corresponds to $\partial\delta_V(t_i^{-1})=-\partial\kappa(t_i)$ in $H^2_D(Y,\mu_\ell)$, in the normalization of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] used in Step 5. For $A=\mathbf Z/\ell$ the scalar map $\mu_\ell\to A(1)$ is an isomorphism and scalar forgetting commutes with the section maps [lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-underlying-comparison]. By Step 4, $\kappa(t_i)=\delta(t_i)$ is a basis of $H^1(V,A(1))$, and by Step 5 $\partial$ is an isomorphism onto $H^2_D(Y,A(1))\cong A$, all other degrees being $0$. So under Step 2 the class of $D$ is a generator, and the stalk of $A_{H_i}\to h_i^!A_X(1)[2]$ at $\bar x$ is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. Since $\bar x$ was arbitrary, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] proves that $A_{H_i}\to h_i^!A_X(1)[2]$ is an isomorphism. The argument applies separately to every $i$ and retains only the trait and invertibility hypotheses.

Computes continuous cohomology of the trivial discrete F_ell-module; generic representation theory, no geometric purity is imported.

Checks a bounded-below derived isomorphism on all geometric cohomology stalks.

Noetherianity of the strict localization and regularity of the strict-local divisor, needed for the ind-etale base change; generic local algebra.
Flatness of etale algebras keeps t_i a nonzerodivisor on the strict localization.
The strict localization is a strictly henselian local ring.
Derived closed adjunction transposing the fundamental class to a supported Ext class.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q63-434ac5972 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read ILO XVI 3.5.11–3.5.13 and the proof of 3.5.12 on printed p.251. The source only cites Illusie 2004 Thm 1.4 and Rapoport–Zink Satz 2.21 for the all-one case. Neither is in literature/, so the WANTED entries and the agent origin are correct. The item statement is unchanged; it is what the monomial parent uses, and it is not weakened. Small cases: n=1 is purity at the closed point of a DVR; the n=2 crossing and the smooth points both follow from absolute purity. No SGA is cited. Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 check out against the cited statements: the regularity of the monomial chart, the étale and torsor argument (roots of unity give unit differences, the monic derivative is invertible, CRT splits the self-product), the descent node plus procyclic two-term giving H^0 = H^1 = A, and the localization cone. Two faults, both repaired in fixes/. (1) Step 2, C1/C4: the reduction from the stalk of h_i^! to supported cohomology on the strict localization had no node for the base change of h^! along Y→X. It also lacked nodes for C Noetherian, for Y and D strictly henselian, and for t_i staying a nonzerodivisor. I added lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change, lem-sbc-strict-hensel-regular-divisor-quotient (with the Mathlib leaf lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base), lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat, lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure and thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint. (2) Step 6, C4/E5: the step claimed that the asd node and the boundary definition 'precisely' give the localization boundary of the Kummer class. They only pin a Yoneda product. I rewrote the step following the accepted Q10 repair: [E] = e_{t^{-1}}, and lem-per-supported-yoneda-localization gives -∂κ(t_i), a generator, with the scalar comparison node. I updated proof_deps and added five tool_uses. New nodes: kummer-tower-acyclic is true (via regular Y_r = C[u]/(u^N - t_i) and transitions killing κ). It is not a restatement of the item and has no duplicate; its future split must avoid absolute, monomial and log purity, or it makes a cycle. procyclic-torsor-tower-descent is true (Hochschild–Serre over the finite levels, then the colimit) and has no duplicate. Batch-5 flags: asd→lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar (a stalk tensor fact), lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base (algebra) and lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian (algebra) are all generic. None of their closures contains a thm-trf or thm-pod node. The nodes added by the repair also add only generic nodes and make no cycle.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
